public_rationale: The forecast concerns the approach that leads to AGI, not whether later models improve on benchmarks. The subsequent capability announcement is material context, but it does not meet the decisive-event rule. Neither current progress nor current limitations establish which approach will deliver the first accepted AGI. With no deadline, the forecast remains open.
limitations: The first accepted AGI is an interpretation of 'lead the way', not a criterion Marcus explicitly supplied.
A hybrid architecture could make attribution disputed even after an accepted AGI demonstration.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs will not be the approach that leads the way to AGI.

statement.excerpt: But between the disappointments of GPT-5 and a new study from METR that shows that LLMs do markedly better on coding benchmarks than in real-word practice, I think it is safe to say that LLMs won’t lead the way.

our_interpretation: In context, 'lead the way' means provide the principal technological approach behind the first broadly accepted AGI systems.
An LLM-based system may include tools, search, reinforcement learning and other components. Their presence alone does not make it a non-LLM approach.
The preceding discussion of GPT-5 and METR supplies reasons for the prediction, not conditional antecedents.
There is no stated deadline. I do not substitute ordinary useful or trustworthy software for the contextual destination of AGI.
criteria.support_condition: The first independently demonstrated, broadly accepted AGI systems principally depend on a non-LLM approach, with technical evidence showing LLMs were not the leading mechanism.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The first independently demonstrated, broadly accepted AGI systems principally depend on LLMs.
